notes:
1. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad — Overview

  • Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was a scholar, journalist, nationalist, Islamic thinker and senior leader of the Indian National Congress.
  • He strongly advocated:
  • Complete Indian independence.
  • Hindu-Muslim unity.
  • Composite nationalism.
  • Secular democracy.
  • Modern education.
  • He became the first Education Minister of independent India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Maulana Azad → Al-Hilal + Congress + Hindu-Muslim Unity + First Education Minister

2. Full Name

  • His name is commonly given as Abul Kalam Ghulam Muhiyuddin Ahmed Azad.
  • He became universally known as Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.

3. Meaning of "Maulana"

  • Maulana is an honorific used for a learned Islamic scholar.

4. Meaning of "Abul Kalam"

  • Abul Kalam means broadly "father/master of discourse."
  • The title reflected his reputation as a scholar and powerful orator.

5. Meaning of "Azad"

  • "Azad" was his pen name.
  • It means "free" or "independent."
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad → Pen Name → "Free"

6. Birth

  • Maulana Azad was born on 11 November 1888.
📌 Must-Memorise

Maulana Azad → 11 November 1888

7. Birthplace

  • He was born in Mecca, then part of the Ottoman Empire.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad → Born in Mecca

8. Family's Return to India

  • His family moved to Calcutta when Azad was still a child.
  • Calcutta became the principal centre of his early intellectual and political life.

9. Father

  • His father was Maulana Khairuddin.
  • He was a respected Islamic scholar.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad's Father → Maulana Khairuddin

10. Education

  • Azad received much of his early education at home.
  • His education included:
  • Arabic.
  • Persian.
  • Urdu.
  • Islamic theology.
  • Philosophy.
  • Mathematics.
  • History.

11. Intellectual Ability

  • Azad demonstrated exceptional linguistic and intellectual ability from a young age.
  • He developed strong interests in:
  • Religion.
  • Philosophy.
  • Politics.
  • Literature.

12. Traditional and Modern Thought

  • Although educated in a traditional Islamic scholarly environment, Azad increasingly engaged with:
  • Modern political ideas.
  • Nationalism.
  • Rational inquiry.
  • Anti-imperialism.

13. Arabic and Persian

  • Azad possessed deep knowledge of Arabic and Persian.
  • He also became one of the most celebrated Urdu prose writers and orators of his generation.

14. Journalism

  • Journalism became one of Azad's most important weapons against British rule.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad → Nationalist Journalism

15. Early Political Influences

  • As a young man, Azad came into contact with revolutionary and anti-colonial ideas.
  • He rejected the belief that Muslims should remain politically separated from the wider Indian nationalist movement.

16. Bengal Revolutionary Context

  • Azad interacted with nationalist circles in Bengal during the period of Swadeshi and revolutionary politics.

17. Opposition to Partition of Bengal

  • The political atmosphere created by the 1905 Partition of Bengal strongly influenced his nationalist thinking.

18. Composite Nationalism

Azad argued that:

  • Hindus and Muslims had lived together in India for centuries.
  • They had created a shared civilisation.
  • Indian nationality could not be divided solely on religious grounds.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad → Composite Nationalism

19. Hindu-Muslim Unity

  • Hindu-Muslim unity was one of the central themes of Azad's entire political career.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad's Core Political Principle → Hindu-Muslim Unity

20. Al-Hilal

  • Maulana Azad founded the Urdu weekly Al-Hilal in Calcutta in 1912.
📌 Must-Memorise

Al-Hilal → 1912 → Maulana Azad

21. Language of Al-Hilal

  • Al-Hilal was published in Urdu.
📌 Must-Memorise

Al-Hilal → Urdu

22. Purpose of Al-Hilal

It promoted:

  • Anti-colonial nationalism.
  • Political awakening.
  • Hindu-Muslim unity.
  • Wider Muslim participation in the freedom struggle.

23. Al-Hilal's Popularity

  • Al-Hilal rapidly became one of the most influential Urdu political journals in India.

24. Style of Al-Hilal

  • Azad's forceful prose and religious-political arguments attracted a large readership.

25. British Reaction

  • British authorities regarded Al-Hilal as politically dangerous.
  • Colonial press laws were used against it.

26. Closure of Al-Hilal

  • The government imposed financial and legal restrictions on the publication.
  • Al-Hilal ceased publication in 1914.
📌 Must-Memorise

Al-Hilal → Started 1912 → Suppressed 1914

27. Al-Balagh

  • After Al-Hilal was suppressed, Azad started another Urdu journal called Al-Balagh.
📌 Must-Memorise

Al-Balagh → Maulana Azad

28. Al-Balagh — Year

  • Al-Balagh began publication in 1915.

29. British Suppression

  • Al-Balagh was also suppressed by the colonial government.
  • Azad's political activity was subjected to increasing restrictions.

30. Internment

  • In 1916, the British government restricted Azad's movement and interned him at Ranchi.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad → Interned at Ranchi → 1916

31. Ranchi Period

  • Azad remained under restrictions at Ranchi for several years.
  • He was released in 1920.
📌 Must-Memorise

Ranchi Internment → 1916–1920

32. First World War Context

  • Azad's anti-British writings became particularly sensitive during the First World War.

33. Islamic World

  • Azad closely followed political developments in the Ottoman Empire and wider Islamic world.
  • However, his nationalism remained rooted in a united Indian political identity.

34. Khilafat Movement

  • After World War I, Azad became an important supporter of the Khilafat Movement.
📌 Must-Memorise

Maulana Azad → Khilafat Movement

35. Khilafat Issue

  • The movement developed around concern for the position of the Ottoman Caliph after World War I.

36. Ali Brothers

Prominent Khilafat leaders included:

  • Mohammad Ali.
  • Shaukat Ali.

37. Gandhi and Khilafat

  • Mahatma Gandhi supported cooperation between the Khilafat and national movements.
  • Azad supported this broad Hindu-Muslim anti-colonial alliance.

38. Congress and Khilafat

  • Congress cooperation with Khilafat helped broaden the social base of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

39. Non-Cooperation Movement

  • Azad became an active leader of Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement beginning in 1920.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad → Non-Cooperation → 1920

40. Boycott Programme

Azad supported:

  • Boycott of colonial institutions.
  • National education.
  • Swadeshi.
  • Non-Cooperation with British rule.

41. Arrest

  • Azad was arrested by the colonial government during the Non-Cooperation phase.

42. Imprisonment

  • Like many major Congress leaders, Azad spent substantial periods in prison during the freedom struggle.

43. Young Congress Leadership

  • By the early 1920s, Azad had become one of the most prominent young leaders of the Indian National Congress.

44. Congress Presidency — 1923

  • Maulana Azad presided over the special session of the Indian National Congress held at Delhi in 1923.
📌 Must-Memorise

1923 Special Delhi Congress → Maulana Azad

45. Youngest Congress President

  • At the time, Azad was among the youngest persons ever to become President of the Indian National Congress.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Maulana Azad → Very Young INC President in 1923

46. Age

  • Azad was about 35 years old when he presided over the 1923 session.

47. Delhi Special Session

  • The session took place during the internal Congress debate over entry into legislative councils.

48. Swarajists vs No-Changers

Swarajists:

  • Favoured entering legislative councils.

No-Changers:

  • Preferred continuation of Gandhian constructive work and council boycott.

49. Azad's Role

  • Azad attempted to maintain Congress unity during internal disputes.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad → Congress Unity

50. C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru

  • C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru led the Swaraj Party.

51. Swaraj Party

  • The Swaraj Party was founded in 1923.
📌 Must-Memorise

Swaraj Party → 1923

52. Azad's Political Position

  • Azad remained committed to:
  • Congress unity.
  • Anti-colonial struggle.
  • Hindu-Muslim cooperation.

53. Communal Tensions

  • The collapse of the Khilafat movement and growth of communal politics deeply concerned Azad.

54. Opposition to Communalism

  • Azad opposed communal mobilisation by both Hindu and Muslim political organisations when it threatened national unity.

55. Muslim League

  • Azad rejected the Muslim League's later theory that Hindus and Muslims constituted two separate nations.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad → Opposed Two-Nation Theory

56. Two-Nation Theory

  • Azad believed religious identity did not automatically create separate national identities.

57. Indian Nationality

For Azad:

  • Indian Muslims were simultaneously:
  • Muslims by religion.
  • Indians by nationality.

58. Common Historical Heritage

  • He argued that centuries of coexistence had created a shared Indian civilisation that could not simply be divided.

59. Salt Satyagraha Period

  • Azad remained involved in Congress nationalist politics during the Civil Disobedience era.

60. Civil Disobedience Movement

  • He supported Gandhi's Civil Disobedience Movement of the 1930s.
  • He was again imprisoned.

61. Gandhi–Irwin Pact

  • Azad participated in the wider Congress debates surrounding the Gandhi–Irwin Pact and constitutional negotiations.

62. Round Table Conference Context

  • Gandhi represented Congress at the Second Round Table Conference.
  • Azad did not serve as Congress's official representative there.

Second Round Table Conference Congress Representative → Gandhi

63. Political Reorganisation During 1930s

  • Azad remained one of the senior figures attempting to preserve broad unity within Congress despite ideological divisions.

64. Congress Socialists

  • The emergence of socialist politics within Congress did not displace Azad's emphasis on nationalism and communal unity.

65. Provincial Elections — 1937

  • Congress performed strongly in the elections held under the Government of India Act 1935.
  • Azad remained an important central Congress leader during this period.

66. Congress Ministries

  • Congress ministries were formed in several provinces beginning in 1937.

67. Second World War

  • The Second World War began in 1939.
  • Britain declared India at war without consulting Indian elected representatives.

68. Congress Ministries Resign

  • Congress ministries resigned in 1939 in protest.
📌 Must-Memorise

Congress Ministries Resigned → 1939

  • Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was elected President of the Indian National Congress at the Ramgarh session in 1940.
📌 Must-Memorise

Ramgarh Congress → 1940 → Maulana Azad

70. Ramgarh Location

  • Ramgarh was then in Bihar and is now in Jharkhand.

71. Second Major Congress Presidency

  • The Ramgarh presidency began Azad's most important phase as Congress president.

  • Because normal Congress elections were disrupted by wartime conditions and mass arrests, Azad continued as Congress president until 1946.
📌 Must-Memorise

During Azad's presidency India witnessed:

  • August Offer.
  • Individual Satyagraha.
  • Cripps Mission.
  • Quit India Movement.
  • World War II.
  • Cabinet Mission negotiations.

74. Longest Continuous Presidency Context

  • Azad's wartime presidency was unusually long because normal organisational functioning was suspended by repression.

75. August Offer

  • Viceroy Lord Linlithgow announced the August Offer in 1940.

76. Congress Response

  • Congress rejected the August Offer as inadequate because it did not provide immediate responsible national government.

77. Individual Satyagraha

  • Gandhi launched Individual Satyagraha in 1940.

78. Vinoba Bhave

  • Vinoba Bhave was selected as the first Individual Satyagrahi.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Individual Satyagrahi → Vinoba Bhave

79. Jawaharlal Nehru

  • Jawaharlal Nehru became the second prominent Individual Satyagrahi.

80. Azad's Role During Individual Satyagraha

  • As Congress president, Azad remained part of the central strategic leadership during the campaign.

81. Cripps Mission

  • Sir Stafford Cripps came to India in March 1942.
📌 Must-Memorise

Cripps Mission → 1942

82. Cripps Mission Purpose

  • Britain sought Indian political cooperation during World War II by offering constitutional proposals for the post-war period.

83. Congress Negotiations

  • As Congress president, Azad played a central role in negotiations with Cripps.
📌 Must-Memorise

Congress President During Cripps Mission → Maulana Azad

84. Why Congress Rejected Cripps

Major concerns included:

  • No immediate transfer of effective power.
  • Defence remained under British control.
  • Provincial opt-out provisions threatened unity.

85. Gandhi's Reaction

  • Gandhi strongly criticised the Cripps proposals as inadequate.

86. Failure of Cripps Mission

  • Negotiations failed in April 1942.

87. Move Toward Quit India

  • Failure of Cripps Mission strengthened the Congress demand for immediate British withdrawal.

88. Quit India Movement

  • The All India Congress Committee adopted the Quit India Resolution on 8 August 1942.
📌 Must-Memorise

Quit India → 8 August 1942

89. Venue

  • The resolution was adopted at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay.

90. "Do or Die"

  • Gandhi gave the famous call "Do or Die."

91. Azad at Quit India Meeting

  • As Congress president, Azad was one of the principal leaders present during the historic 1942 deliberations.
📌 Must-Memorise

INC President During Quit India → Maulana Azad

92. Arrest

  • Azad and almost the entire top Congress leadership were arrested on 9 August 1942.

93. Ahmednagar Fort

  • Azad was imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort along with several other senior Congress leaders.
📌 Must-Memorise

Azad → Ahmednagar Fort → Quit India Imprisonment

94. Fellow Prisoners

Senior nationalist leaders imprisoned there included figures such as:

  • Jawaharlal Nehru.
  • Vallabhbhai Patel.
  • Other Congress Working Committee members.

95. Duration

  • Azad remained imprisoned for much of the Quit India period.
  • He was released in 1945.

96. Personal Tragedy

  • Azad's wife died while he was imprisoned during the wartime period.
  • He was unable to be with her during her final illness.

97. Ghubar-e-Khatir

  • During imprisonment, Azad wrote a series of letters later published as Ghubar-e-Khatir.
📌 Must-Memorise

Ghubar-e-Khatir → Maulana Azad

98. Nature of Ghubar-e-Khatir

The work contains reflections on:

  • Religion.
  • Philosophy.
  • Culture.
  • Literature.
  • Personal experience.

99. Urdu Prose

  • Ghubar-e-Khatir is regarded as an important work of modern Urdu prose.

100. Release in 1945

  • The release of Congress leaders reopened negotiations over India's political future.

101. Wavell Plan

  • Viceroy Lord Wavell proposed a reconstitution of his Executive Council in 1945.

102. Simla Conference

  • The Simla Conference was held in 1945.
📌 Must-Memorise

Simla Conference → 1945

103. Azad at Simla

  • As Congress president, Azad represented Congress in major negotiations at Simla.

104. Main Dispute at Simla

  • A major issue concerned Muslim representation and the Muslim League's claim to be the sole representative of Indian Muslims.

105. Azad's Position

  • Azad rejected the League's claim that all Muslims politically belonged to one communal organisation.

106. Failure of Simla Conference

  • The conference failed to produce agreement between Congress, the Muslim League and the British government.

107. Cabinet Mission

  • The Cabinet Mission came to India in 1946.
📌 Must-Memorise

Cabinet Mission → 1946

108. Cabinet Mission Members

The three British Cabinet members were:

  • Lord Pethick-Lawrence.
  • Sir Stafford Cripps.
  • A.V. Alexander.
📌 Must-Memorise

Cabinet Mission → Pethick-Lawrence + Cripps + A.V. Alexander

109. Azad and Cabinet Mission

  • Azad played a major role in Congress negotiations with the Cabinet Mission.
📌 Must-Memorise

Congress President During Cabinet Mission Negotiations → Azad

110. Azad's Preference

  • Azad strongly preferred a united India.
  • He regarded the Cabinet Mission Plan as a possible framework for avoiding Partition.

111. Cabinet Mission Plan

It proposed broadly:

  • A Union handling limited central subjects.
  • Provincial groupings.
  • A Constituent Assembly.

112. Azad and Federation

  • Azad was willing to consider significant provincial autonomy if it could preserve Indian unity.

113. Congress Internal Differences

  • Congress leaders disagreed on some interpretations of the Cabinet Mission Plan.

114. Jinnah and Muslim League

  • Muhammad Ali Jinnah increasingly insisted on the creation of Pakistan.

  • United India.

  • He supported educational expansion for women.
